summary: Add a daily UTC alert-creation trend endpoint with counts by severity.
scope_anchors: days query parameter: default 7, minimum 1, maximum 90
UTC calendar-day bucket generation and oldest-first ordering
zero-count days and Low/Medium/High/Critical severity fields
exact_source_files_note: Seven files are required because this story adds both request and response contracts in addition to the existing five-layer endpoint path; this is a genuinely broader slice than the compact default.
adjacent_dependencies: AlertService.Common/Enums/Severity.cs for Low, Medium, High, Critical ordering
AlertService.API/Program.cs for TimeProvider registration and service composition
AlertService.Models/Alert.cs for CreatedDate and Severity persistence fields
constraints: Keep controller -> service -> repository layering and async cancellation behavior.
Use UTC boundaries from the existing TimeProvider path; do not use local machine time.
Use set-based, parameterized EF/SQL aggregation over the CreatedDate range and review index implications.
Use existing Severity ordering and response naming conventions: Low, Medium, High, Critical.
Let ASP.NET Core query model validation produce the existing ValidationProblemDetails shape.
No schema or migration change is expected unless implementation evidence disproves this.
Full dotnet test may include unrelated ALERT-411/ALERT-412 integration expectations; use focused commands while implementing this slice.
assumptions: Unless product confirms otherwise, last N days includes today: UTC range [today - (N - 1) days, tomorrow).
Unless product confirms otherwise, each bucket exposes an ISO yyyy-MM-dd calendar date field.
Missing dates and severities are materialized by the service as zeroes, while the repository returns grouped existing rows.
coverage_goals: Default days is 7; values 1 and 90 are accepted; 0, 91, and non-numeric input produce 400 ValidationProblemDetails.
UTC boundary dates are included/excluded correctly and buckets are oldest first.
Empty days and missing severities are returned with zero counts.
Mixed alerts map to correct total and Low/Medium/High/Critical daily counts.
missing_facts: Product confirmation of whether the current UTC day is included is missing.
Product confirmation of the trend bucket date representation is missing.
unresolved_questions: Does last N days include the current UTC day?
What exact date representation should the response contract expose?
